Crispy Chicken Tacos for the Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe

Served at: Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe

Serves 6-8 (makes 12-18 tacos)Prep 30 minCook 40 min

Crispy Tacos, known as Tacos Dorados in Mexico, are a beloved festive dish, often gracing tables during celebrations like the Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe on December 12th. These golden, crunchy tacos, typically filled with savory shredded chicken or potato, are a comforting and joyful addition to any family gathering, symbolizing the warmth and tradition of Mexican cuisine.

Ingredients

  • 1 pound (450g) boneless, skinless chicken breasts or thighs
  • 1/2 white onion, quartered
  • 2 cloves garlic, smashed
  • 1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
  • 1/2 teaspoon black pepper, plus more to taste
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
  • 1/4 teaspoon dried oregano
  • 12-18 corn tortillas (6-inch / 15 cm)
  • 3-4 cups (700-950 ml) vegetable oil, for frying
  • For serving:
  • 1 head iceberg or romaine lettuce, shredded
  • 1 cup (115g) crumbled queso fresco or cotija cheese
  • 1 cup (240 ml) salsa roja or verde
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) Mexican crema or sour cream

Method

  1. Place chicken, onion quarters, and smashed garlic cloves in a medium pot. Cover with water by about 1 inch (2.5 cm). Add 1 teaspoon salt and 1/2 teaspoon black pepper.
  2. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through and easily shreddable.
  3. Remove chicken from the pot, reserving about 1/4 cup (60 ml) of the cooking liquid. Let chicken cool slightly, then shred it using two forks.
  4. In a bowl, combine the shredded chicken with the ground cumin, dried oregano, and 2-3 tablespoons of the reserved cooking liquid. Mix well and taste, adjusting salt and pepper if needed.
  5. Warm the corn tortillas to make them pliable. You can do this by heating them briefly in a microwave (stacked, covered with a damp paper towel, for 30-60 seconds) or on a dry griddle for 15-20 seconds per side.
  6. Place about 1-2 tablespoons of the shredded chicken filling near one edge of each warm tortilla. Roll the tortilla tightly into a cylinder.
  7. If desired, secure each rolled taco with a toothpick to prevent it from unraveling during frying. (This step is optional, as they often stay rolled once fried).
  8. In a large, heavy-bottomed skillet or Dutch oven, heat the vegetable oil over medium-high heat until it reaches 350-375°F (175-190°C). If you don't have a thermometer, a small piece of tortilla should sizzle immediately when dropped in.
  9. Carefully place 3-4 rolled tacos into the hot oil, seam-side down first. Fry for 2-3 minutes per side, or until golden brown and crispy.
  10. Remove fried tacos with tongs and place them on a wire rack set over a baking sheet lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
  11. Repeat with the remaining tacos, ensuring the oil temperature stays consistent.
  12. Remove any toothpicks before serving. Arrange the crispy tacos on a platter and top generously with shredded lettuce, crumbled queso fresco, salsa roja or verde, and a drizzle of Mexican crema or sour cream.

Tips

  • For a vegetarian option, replace chicken with seasoned mashed potatoes or black beans.
  • To make ahead, prepare the chicken filling and shred the lettuce. Fry the tacos just before serving for maximum crispiness.
  • Serve with a side of refried beans and Mexican rice for a complete festive meal.
